questions.q: Household linen is generally categorized based on the area of the house it is used. Which of the following falls under 'bathroom linen'?
options: Table mats
Bed sheets
Towels and washcloths
Curtains and draperies
questions.explain: Bathroom linen includes items used for personal hygiene and drying in the bathroom, such as bath towels, face towels, and washcloths.

questions.q: When selecting a bath towel for household use, which of the following fabric properties is the most important to consider?
options: Transparency
Absorbency
Reflectiveness
Stiffness
questions.explain: The primary function of a towel is to dry the body, so it must be highly absorbent to quickly soak up water.

questions.q: The clothing repair method used to mend a torn or snagged area by weaving yarn across the hole is called:
options: Darning
Patching
Tacking
Hemming
questions.explain: Darning is a sewing technique for repairing small holes or worn areas in fabric by interlacing thread across the hole, similar to weaving.

questions.q: Patching differs from darning because patching involves:
options: Using glue to stick two loose threads together.
Applying a piece of matching or contrasting fabric over a large hole.
Using a hot iron to melt the fabric back together.
Weaving thin threads over tiny holes in socks.
questions.explain: Patching is the process of sewing a separate piece of material over a larger hole or worn area to cover it, whereas darning uses only thread.

questions.q: Why is it highly recommended to 'air' clothes that have just been worn but are not dirty enough to wash?
options: To allow sunlight to fade their colors.
To evaporate body moisture (sweat) and prevent foul odors and mildew.
To make them easier to cut for patching.
To permanently set the dirt into the fabric.
questions.explain: Airing worn clothes helps body sweat evaporate, keeps the clothes fresh, and prevents the growth of odor-causing bacteria and mildew.

questions.q: When storing woolen clothing in a wardrobe or box for a long time, it is advisable to use mothballs (camphor). What is the purpose of this?
options: To make the wool shrink properly.
To bleach the woolen clothes to a bright white.
To repel fabric-eating insects like moths.
To increase the weight of the wool.
questions.explain: Mothballs or camphor emit a strong odor that acts as an insecticide/repellent, protecting natural protein fibers like wool from moth larvae that feed on them.
